claims.proposition_evaluated: At its meeting of 2026-08-26 (item 7.6) the Infrastructure Committee rejected Recommendation 1 (R) of report IS03688. Rejected means a motion to adopt R was put and defeated, or a motion incompatible with R was carried. The claim also requires that R proposed a hold under claim 2's primary deferral definition, and that City Council had not adopted R by 2026-09-25.
claims.interpretation_notes: TREATMENT FIRST. The agenda-adoption motion at 1.4 (moved by R. Clarke, carried 6-0) replaced Attachment 5 with both 'Version 1' and 'Version 2'. The open-data text does not say which of the two was before the committee when it considered item 7.6. I therefore use Version 2 (DocumentId 304030) as the declared primary reading. Under my claim-2 reading, Version 2 does not expressly defer the 14 listed routes. It says they 'will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications', that a Q1 2027 report will come 'for Council direction and approval', and that they 'may be re-evaluated using alternate design approaches'. So the no-hold ladder applies. The original (304032) and Version 1 (304031) do propose a hold: the original removes the routes 'from the scope ... for 2026 and 2027', and Version 1 says they 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed'. DISPOSITION. The City's 2025-2029 open-data voting records (two datasets) show no motion at 7.6 that would adopt R. The only substantive motion was moved by A. Salvador and was incompatible with R: continue the programme within the approved scope of CM-20-0330, send tender-ready routes to procurement now, and be ready to build in 2027. It was DEFEATED 2-2 (Janz and Salvador yes; Clarke and Rutherford no; Knack and Paquette absent). An amendment by E. Rutherford to delete 'and maximize remaining construction season, including advancing partial and accelerated construction' from Part 2 was also DEFEATED 2-2 (Clarke and Rutherford yes; Janz and Salvador no; Knack and Paquette absent). No motion adopting R was carried and no incompatible motion was carried, so R was LEFT WITHOUT A DECISION. Media report that the report was 'received for information'. The ladder gives Partially supported whether or not R proposed a hold, so the verdict does not depend on which version was operative. What is established: the committee did not take up R. What is not established: that members voted R down, or voted to go ahead against it. Under Version 2, it is also not established that what was declined was a hold. ALTERNATIVE READING ('did not support' = non-adoption): Supported, because no body adopted R by 2026-09-25. ALTERNATIVE BODY (City Council): I found nothing showing that R or IS03688 came before Council by 2026-09-25, so for Council the result is Not established; a body that did not receive R cannot have rejected it. The only Council vote in the period that mentions active transportation is on 2026-09-15 (public hearing, item 2.1), which set a new due date for report UPE02721 on Charter Bylaws 24007 and 24008. Carried 13-0; it is not R. Coun. Salvador's motion seeking funding options for active transportation in the 2027-2030 budget was listed as pending on the 2026-09-08 selection sheet, per Taproot, 2026-09-14. OVERRIDE STRAND: the committee made no decision on R, and I found no later, incompatible Council decision, so the record shows no override. Commenters who said Council 'ignore[d] a committee's decision' are not borne out; the committee made no decision to ignore. COMMITTEE: the open-data voter columns show Clarke, Janz, Knack (Mayor), Paquette, Rutherford and Salvador as voting members. The committee also carried 4-0 (moved by Rutherford) that Attachment 4 remain private. WHAT GOVERNED AFTERWARDS: the previously approved scope of CM-20-0330. I found no later Council decision changing it. Administration's own statements, relayed by Taproot from the City project page, say Grovenor was cancelled, 101 Avenue (Terrace Heights) was moved to next year, and 95 Avenue was deferred. These are administration statements, not Council decisions.

claims.proposition_evaluated: In report IS03688 (Infrastructure Committee, 2026-08-26), administration recommended an approach that expressly defers construction or advancement of 14 named, unbuilt routes of the programme until a further evaluation, report or decision. Tested on Version 2 of Attachment 5 as the declared operative version.
claims.interpretation_notes: Operative version: the 1.4 agenda-adoption motion replaced 'Attachments 2, 3, 5 (Version 1) and 5 (Version 2)' and does not identify which version was before the committee, so Version 2 (304030) is primary. The same 14 route entries are listed apart in all three versions: 50 Street (101 Avenue to 109A Avenue); 64 Street (119 Avenue to Yellowhead Trail); 79 Street (76 Avenue to 101 Avenue); 84 Avenue (79 Street to 83 Street); 85 Street (93 Avenue to 98 Avenue); 88 Avenue/93 Street/87 Avenue (85 Street to 96 Street); 89 Street (76 Avenue to Connors Road); 92A Avenue/86 Street/alley (Connors Road to 85 Street); 93 Street (82 Avenue to 84 Avenue) and 84 Avenue (91 Street to 89 Street); 93 Avenue/82 Street/94 Avenue (85 Street to 75 Street) and 75 Street (94 Avenue to 94B Avenue); 95 Avenue (142 Street to 163 Street); 101 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); 106 Avenue (50 Street to west of 84 Street); Grovenor - 148 Street, 104 Avenue and 144 Street. Count = 14 by entry. If entries joined by 'and' or by the Grovenor bullet were split, the count would be 18. The 'continue as planned' list has 13 entries in every version (14 if '110 Avenue/90 Street ... and 112 Avenue' were split). CLASSIFICATION BY VERSION. ORIGINAL (304032): the listed projects 'would be removed from the scope of the Active Transportation Network Expansion Program for 2026 and 2027', to be possibly revisited after administration evaluates changes in bike-lane authority and funding. Meets the primary reading and the stricter reading. VERSION 1 (304031): routes not yet constructed 'would be evaluated to determine if they should proceed', and routes impacting travel lanes or parking 'will be removed'. The list passage itself says only that the listed projects 'may be revisited'. Meets the primary reading, because the routes wait on the evaluation. Does not meet the stricter reading in terms for the listed routes, because the text never says these routes meet criteria 1a or 1b. VERSION 2 (304030): 'The remaining routes will be evaluated for trade-offs, alternative design treatments and budget implications', with a Q1 2027 report 'for Council direction and approval', and the listed projects 'may be re-evaluated'. The text contains no word of deferral, removal or waiting. That is evaluation plus a report back, so it does NOT meet the primary reading, and does not meet the stricter reading. This is a textual judgement; the contrast with routes that 'will continue as planned' implies the others will not, but implication is not express deferral. STATUS: Attachment 3 (304029 and 304028) is not carried in this package and returned 403, so the status of every listed route at the primary date (as of 2026-08-10) is unresolved. For the alternative date (2026-08-26), Attachment 5 itself, a City record dated for the 2026-08-26 committee, confines the approach to routes that 'have not yet started construction' and puts routes 'already under construction' on the continue list. By the attachment's own classification, all 14 had not started construction. VERDICT: under Version 2 the primary deferral element fails, so the result is Partially supported. Under the original or Version 1, the count and deferral hold. The result would be Not established at the primary status date (unresolved status is the only obstacle) and Supported at the alternative status date. The finding is VERSION-SENSITIVE and STATUS-DATE-SENSITIVE. Separately, the report body (not Attachment 5 and not R) says that for all routes where construction has not started, 'construction is best postponed to 2027'. That covers continuing routes too.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Between 2022-11-30 and 2026-09-25, Councillors Karen Principe and Jennifer Rice brought two motions at City Council that would leave about $45-55 million in capital profile CM-20-0330 and direct the released funds to named destinations, and Council defeated both.
claims.interpretation_notes: Two candidate motions were found. Both were moved by K. Principe and seconded by J. Rice, on separate occasions, so they count as jointly brought under both the primary and the co-sponsorship reading of 'brought'. MOTION 1: City Council Budget, 2023-11-21, item 5.1.2. 'That capital profile CM-20-0330 - Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 be reduced by $50,000,000', phased $16,350,000 (2024), $16,825,000 (2025) and $16,825,000 (2026). Per the open-data summary, the funding source reduced is Tax-Supported Debt. DEFEATED 4-8. Reviewer's arithmetic: 16.35 + 16.825 + 16.825 = $50.0M. Base $100,000,000, from Capital Budget Amendment 7, 2022-11-30; I could not read the capital profile or spring 2023 adjustments. Remainder $50.0M: meets the primary band (45-55) and the alternative (at least half). Destination: a reduction in tax-supported borrowing, which meets 'a reduction in borrowing' if the minutes' wording matches the open-data text. MOTION 2: City Council Budget, 2024-12-02, item 5.1.2. Reduce CM-20-0330 by $33,650,000 in 2025 and $33,650,000 in 2026, funding source Tax-Supported Debt, 'to defund planning, design and delivery of the Active Transportation Implementation Acceleration - Approach 3 project'. DEFEATED 4-7. Reviewer's arithmetic: 2 x 33.65 = $67.3M. On a $100M base the remainder is $32.7M. That fails the primary band and meets the alternative. The base could not be read from the capital profile. For the remainder to fall in 45-55, the approved total would have had to be $112.3M-$122.3M. That is inconsistent with the 2026 report IS03688, which describes the approval as $100 million and says the profile was unchanged. The two cuts equal exactly the 2025 and 2026 annual amounts approved in 2022, so the motion appears to remove all funding for those two years. Destination: tax-supported debt, i.e. a reduction in borrowing. CBC (2024-12-05, seen only as a search-result summary, not opened) described it as moving $67M 'toward the tax levy'. The minutes should settle the wording. Result: two jointly brought reduction motions were defeated, but only one meets the primary amount band, so Supported does not apply and the verdict is Partially supported. Under the alternative band (at least half), both motions qualify, and Supported would follow if the destinations hold. The finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE on the amount band. OTHER MOTIONS (qualification 4): City Council, 2025-09-16, item 10.13, 'Bike Lane Implementation Suspension and Review', moved by T. Cartmell and seconded by K. Principe, to cease construction on bike lane projects pending review. DEFEATED 4-9; Rice and Principe voted yes. It proposed a pause, not a budget reduction, and named no amount. Principe and Rice also voted against the 2022 approval and the borrowing bylaws.

claims.suggested_one_line: Principe and Rice did twice move to cut the bike-lane budget and lost both times. The 2023 motion would have left $50 million; the 2024 motion would have left about $33 million.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Mostly. Coun. Principe moved, and Coun. Rice seconded, two cuts to the $100-million programme. In November 2023, a $50-million cut would have left $50 million; defeated 4-8. In December 2024, a $67.3-million cut, removing the 2025 and 2026 funding, would have left about $32.7 million on the original $100 million; defeated 4-7. Both reduced tax-supported borrowing. Only the first matches 'cut it to $50M'.
suggested_tldr: Two motions, both Principe/Rice, both defeated: 2023-11-21 (4-8) and 2024-12-02 (4-7).
2023: leave $50M. 2024: leave about $32.7M (reviewer's calculation on a $100M base).
Both released the money by reducing tax-supported debt.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Across City Council's recorded votes on funding or continuing CM-20-0330 from 2022-11-30 to 2026-09-25 (vote set V), at least seven members (the mayor counted) who served both before and after the October 2025 election each cast at least one vote in V in each term, and voted on the programme's side at every V vote held while they served.
claims.interpretation_notes: V as found (all City Council, all in the 2021-2025 term). V1: 2022-11-30 CBA 7, approve $100M, carried 9-4, pro = yes. V2: 2022-11-30 item 13.84, operating impacts of CBA 7, carried 10-3, pro = yes; included as a candidate because it funds the programme's operating costs; excluding it changes nothing. V3: 2023-03-14 Bylaw 20394 first reading, carried 8-4, pro = yes. V4 and V5: 2023-04-17 Bylaw 20394 second and third readings, each carried 8-4, pro = yes. V6: 2023-11-21 cut $50M, defeated 4-8, pro = no. V7: 2023-11-21 item 5.1.3, the bundled Fall 2023 Supplemental Capital Budget Adjustment motion, including 'the exception for capital profile CM-20-0330' in Attachment 11, carried 11-2. V7 is UNCLASSIFIABLE because I could not read Attachment 11 to establish the exception's effect. V8: 2024-12-02 cut $67.3M, defeated 4-7, pro = no. V9: 2025-08-19 Bylaw 21265 (amending Bylaw 20394) first reading, carried 12-1, pro = yes. V10 and V11: 2025-09-16 Bylaw 21265 second and third readings, each carried 10-3, pro = yes. V12: 2025-09-16 item 10.13 suspension motion (Cartmell/Principe), defeated 4-9, pro = no. V holds NO vote in the 2025-2029 term. The 2025-2029 open data shows no Council motion on CM-20-0330 funding or continuation through 2026-09-25. The December 2025 budget amendment found concerned transit bike racks under CM-66-3600, which is not this programme. PRIMARY RULE: under the both-terms condition nobody can qualify, so B = 0 for want of a vote, and the brief's rule gives NOT ESTABLISHED (the 2025-2029 term holds no vote in V). Assessability is met: 11 classified votes, which passes both the 3-vote and 2-vote minima. PER-MEMBER COUNTS in V (2021-25 term; pro / contrary / absent / unclassifiable cast): Knack 11/0/0/1; Paquette 10/0/1/1 (not recorded at V8); Salvador 11/0/0/1; Sohi (mayor) 9/0/2/1 (absent V4, V5); Stevenson 11/0/0/1; Rutherford 10/1/0/1 (voted for the V8 cut); Wright 10/0/1/1 (absent V3); Tang 11/0/0/1; Janz 10/0/1/1 (absent V6); Rice 1/10/0/1; Principe 0/11/0/1; Hamilton 3/7/1/1; Cartmell 2/9/0/1. 2025-2029 term: 0 votes in V for any member. ALTERNATIVES UNDER V. (i) While-serving, absence breaks: upper 4 (Knack, Salvador, Stevenson, Tang), lower 0 (every member cast a vote on V7), so the counts fall in different bands and the result is Not established. If V7 were excluded or classified pro, B = 4: Partially supported under the primary bands, Contradicted under the alternative bands. Without the mayor, also 4. (ii) Less strict absence rule without both-terms: upper 8 (Knack, Paquette, Salvador, Sohi, Stevenson, Wright, Tang, Janz; 7 without the mayor), lower 0, so Not established. If V7 were excluded or classified pro: 8, Supported (7 without the mayor, also Supported). (iii) Less strict with both-terms: Not established (no 2025-29 vote). V+ adds the Infrastructure Committee votes of 2026-08-26 on item 7.6. Salvador's motion to continue: pro = yes; Janz and Salvador pro; Clarke and Rutherford contrary; Knack and Paquette absent. Rutherford's deletion amendment: pro = no; the same split. The 2026-07-07 Council vote on the 50 Street design is excluded, because its text does not say which way it cuts. The 2026-06-30 Executive Committee motion to pause 50 Street is excluded because it is a single-route committee vote. V+ primary (both terms): upper 1 (Salvador; Knack and Paquette cast no 2025-29 V+ vote, Janz was absent at V6, Rutherford contrary), lower 0. Both counts are 3 or fewer, so Contradicted under both band sets. V+ while-serving: upper 3 (Salvador, Stevenson, Tang), lower 0, so Contradicted under both band sets. V+ less strict with both-terms: upper 2 (Salvador, Janz), so Contradicted. V+ less strict without both-terms: upper 8, lower 0, so Not established. The finding is DEFINITION-SENSITIVE. Largest pro-programme count in a single classified V vote: 12 (V9). Smallest: 7 (V8). Continuing members on the Council elected in October 2025 (from the 2025-2029 voter lists): Knack (now mayor), Paquette, Salvador, Stevenson, Rutherford, Wright, Principe, Tang, Janz. New: Clarke, Elliott, Morgan, Parmar. Not returning: Sohi, Rice, Hamilton, Cartmell. The one fixed group visible in 2021-2025 is the nine who voted to approve the programme in 2022. Only Knack, Salvador, Stevenson and Tang voted with the programme at every classified V vote with no absence. This is a pattern in a vote table and says nothing about intention or coordination.

claims.suggested_one_line: The record cannot show a continuing bloc of seven, because Council has held no vote on the programme's funding since the October 2025 election. In 2021-2025, only four members backed the programme at every such vote without missing one.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Not established. City Council held 12 recorded votes on funding or continuing the bike-lane programme between November 2022 and September 2025, and none in the term that began after the October 2025 election. So no one can be shown to belong to a bloc spanning both councils. In the 2021-2025 term, nine members approved the programme in 2022. Knack, Salvador, Stevenson and Tang then voted with the programme at every classifiable vote without an absence. Others missed a vote, and Rutherford voted for the 2024 cut. The figure is seven or eight only if single absences are forgiven. This is a pattern in a vote table and says nothing about why anyone voted as they did.
suggested_tldr: No Council vote on the programme's funding since the October 2025 election, so the 'same' bloc across both councils cannot be tested.
2021-2025: four members voted with the programme at every classifiable vote; eight did if single absences are forgiven.
Rutherford voted for the 2024 cut; the pro-programme side ranged from 7 to 12 votes.
